_what: How tool:route-buttons and tool:find-nearest-places (read-data/get-there.mjs) open a trip and find places. `maps` are the maps apps a button opens, each an address template over the encoded fields (a stop is a place's address or its latitude,longitude): a new maps app is a row. `places` says where places are read: `geocode` turns words into a point and `near` lists places around a point by brand (`near_query`), and by name (`near_query_by_name`) when no place carries that brand, and by the address service's own search inside a box around the start (`near_by_search`) when every copy of the places service is busy (OpenStreetMap's open services, no account; `near` lists several copies of the same service, asked in turn when one is busy), each with its address template and `user_agent`, which those services ask every caller to send. Each map row's `modes` maps the travel modes a caller may name to that app's own word. `most` caps how many places come back; `radius_km` is how far around the start is searched unless the caller says; `most_at_most` and `radius_km_at_most` bound what a caller may ask. `words` are what the answer says.

words.found: {count} {name} near {start}; the nearest is {nearest}, {km} km away.
words.start_unknown: Could not find where {start} is. Give a fuller address or a latitude and longitude.
words.no_destination: Say where to go: an address, a place name, or a latitude and longitude.
